quizName: DMV Practice Test #15 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks while braking, what should you do?

options.text: Release the brake until the rear tire grips again, then brake again.
Release the brake and use only the front brake.
Keep the brake locked until the motorcycle stops.
Release the brake and coast to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the brake locked until the motorcycle stops.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while braking, do not release the brake. Keep it locked until you stop completely.

questions.question: How long can the effects of marijuana last?

options.text: No more than 15 minutes.
About one hour.
About two hours.
More than six hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: More than six hours.
questions.explanation: Smoked marijuana affects users within minutes and lasts two to four hours. Eaten marijuana takes over an hour to start working but can last more than six hours.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT affect a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: The amount of alcohol consumed
Body weight
How fast the alcohol was consumed
How often alcohol is consumed

questions.correctAnswerText: How often alcohol is consumed
questions.explanation: Three main factors affect BAC: the amount of alcohol consumed, how fast it was consumed, and body weight. Sex, physical condition, and food intake also matter. How often you drink does not.

questions.question: When being passed, why should you not move to the far side of your lane?

options.text: The passing vehicle may come back into your lane too soon.
You may block another vehicle from passing you.
The side nearest the passing vehicle is safer.
You will feel more wind blast from the passing vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The passing vehicle may come back into your lane too soon.
questions.explanation: Do not ride on the far side of your lane when being passed. This might tempt the other driver to return to your lane before it is safe.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When traffic is light.
When traffic is heavy.
When you can see through vehicles ahead.
When the weather is clear and pleasant.

questions.correctAnswerText: When traffic is heavy.
questions.explanation: A two-second following distance is usually okay. Increase it when you need more time to stop, such as in heavy traffic, bad weather, at night, or when you cannot see ahead.

questions.question: What can help reduce your reaction time?

options.text: Ride slower than the speed limit.
Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
Shift into neutral when slowing down.
Pull in the clutch when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes to reduce reaction time. This is especially useful when riding through areas with potential hazards.

questions.question: Where should you ride when being passed from behind?

options.text: In the center of the lane.
In the left part of the lane.
In the right part of the lane.
Anywhere in the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: Stay in the center of your lane when being passed. This discourages the other driver from returning to your lane before it is safe.

questions.question: Should you use your headlight during the day?

options.text: No.
Yes, on high beam.
Yes, on low beam.
Yes, switch between high and low beam.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, on high beam.
questions.explanation: Use your high beam headlight during the day to help other drivers see you. Use high beam anytime you are not following or approaching other vehicles.

questions.question: When riding a three-wheeled motorcycle through a curve, what is best?

options.text: Stay in the center of the lane.
Stay on the outside of the lane.
Adjust your path as needed.
Use the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Adjust your path as needed.
questions.explanation: Three-wheeled motorcycles handle curves differently than two-wheeled motorcycles. You may need to move from the outside to the inside of a curve, or adjust your path in other ways to stay safe.

questions.question: What can increase fatigue while riding?

options.text: Stopping frequently.
Riding in cool, windy weather.
Being comfortable on your motorcycle.
Starting your ride late in the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding in cool, windy weather.
questions.explanation: Dress to protect yourself from tiring weather like wind and rain. Limit rides to about six hours per day and take a break every two hours. Avoid artificial stimulants because you may feel very tired when they wear off.

questions.question: When riding, what should you do?

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your arms straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes to look where you are going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look where you are going.
questions.explanation: When turning, look where you want to go by turning only your head and eyes. Keep your knees against the gas tank to maintain balance while turning. Your arms should be slightly bent when holding the handgrips.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, which part of the lane should you use?

options.text: The left portion of the lane
The center portion of the lane
The right portion of the lane
Either the left or right portion of the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: The left portion of the lane
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when passing parked cars. This keeps you farthest away from opening car doors, people stepping out between cars, and cars pulling out of parking spaces.

questions.question: More than half of all crashes:

options.text: Occur at speeds greater than 35 mph.
Happen at night.
Are caused by worn tires.
Involve riders with less than six months of experience on their motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Involve riders with less than six months of experience on their motorcycle.
questions.explanation: More than half of all motorcycle crashes involve riders who have had their motorcycle for less than six months.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what should riders do?

options.text: Spread out to make the group easier to see.
Stay close together to make the group easier to see.
Separate occasionally.
Ride in pairs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay close together to make the group easier to see.
questions.explanation: Riders in a group should stay close together while leaving enough space to maneuver. This makes the group easier to see and prevents riders from getting separated. Do not ride in pairs because this does not leave enough room to maneuver.

questions.question: If you need to brake while in a curve, what should you do?

options.text: Brake more gradually than you would on a straight road.
Brake as hard as you would on a straight road.
Wait until you are not in the curve to brake.
Only use the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake more gradually than you would on a straight road.
questions.explanation: Tires have less grip when a motorcycle is leaning than when it is upright. Try to straighten your motorcycle before braking. If you must brake while turning, apply the brakes more gently and gradually than on a straight road.

questions.question: In traffic, how much stopping distance does a motorcycle need compared to a car?

options.text: Much less distance to stop than cars.
Less distance to stop than cars.
As much distance to stop as cars.
More distance to stop than cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: As much distance to stop as cars.
questions.explanation: In traffic, a motorcycle needs as much stopping distance as a car.

questions.question: To carry a passenger, what may you need to adjust?

options.text: The shocks.
The handlebars.
The brakes.
The throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The shocks.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to the motorcycle, so you may need to adjust the shocks. You should also adjust the headlight and mirrors because the motorcycle will sit at a different angle with the extra weight.

questions.question: To stop quickly, what should you do?

options.text: Use only the rear brake.
Use only the front brake.
Use both brakes.
Use the rear brake firmly while gradually increasing the front brake pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, which instruction should you NOT give?

options.text: Get on the motorcycle after the engine has been started.
Sit as far forward as you can without crowding me.
Hold firmly onto my waist, hips, or belt.
Feel free to talk whenever you want.

questions.correctAnswerText: Feel free to talk whenever you want.
questions.explanation: Passengers should not talk or move around while the motorcycle is moving. This helps you stay focused on riding. Passengers should get on only after the engine starts. They should sit as far forward as possible without crowding you and hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: How can a motorcyclist stop other vehicles from lane sharing?

options.text: Ride in the left portion of a lane.
Ride in the center portion of a lane.
Give dirty looks if another driver moves into your lane.
Ride in a zigzag pattern to fill up the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center portion of a lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center portion of your lane to discourage other drivers from trying to squeeze in next to you.

questions.question: When turning on a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Press the grip in the direction you want to turn.
Press the grip opposite the direction you want to turn.
Do not hold the grip because it is dangerous.
Do not lean the motorcycle because it is unsafe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the grip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: At speeds faster than walking, your motorcycle must lean to turn. Press the grip in the direction you want to turn. This will make the motorcycle lean the right way.

questions.question: When riding a three-wheeled motorcycle or with a sidecar, why should you not ride too far to the right of your lane?

options.text: Other drivers may not see you.
You will not pass other vehicles as easily.
Other drivers may try to share your lane.
You may run off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may run off the road.
questions.explanation: A sidecar sits on the right side of a motorcycle. If you ride too far to the right, the sidecar can run off the road. On a three-wheeled motorcycle, the rear right wheel may leave the road if you get too close to the right edge.

questions.question: When riding through a turn, how should you look?

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your arms straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes to look through turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look through turns.
questions.explanation: Look through a turn toward where you want to go. Turn only your head to look, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: When riding in a group, where should inexperienced riders position themselves?

options.text: In the front of the group.
Right behind the leader.
At the back of the group.
Wherever they are most comfortable.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader near the front of the group. This allows experienced riders at the back to watch them and help if needed.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid hitting an object in the road, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up before contact.
Slow down before contact.
Lean the motorcycle.
Stay seated on the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before contact.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid an obstacle, slow down as much as you can before hitting it. Try to hit it at a 90-degree angle. Keep your motorcycle upright. Rise slightly off your seat and roll the throttle back a little before impact to lighten the front end.
